Done. Summary of the move:

- `backend/pdftest/pdftest.go` → `backend/testutils/pdf.go` (package renamed `pdftest` → `testutils`); `app_test.go`, `backend/filetree/filetree_test.go`, `backend/pdf/pdf_test.go` updated accordingly.
- `backend/drive/testutils_test.go` → folded into `backend/testutils/drive.go` as exported `SkipUnlessDriveEnabled`; `auth_test.go`, `folders_test.go`, `upload_test.go` in `backend/drive` now call that instead of the old package-private `skipUnlessEnabled`.

One nuance worth flagging: `skipUnlessEnabled` used to call `drive.configDir()` directly. Moving it into `testutils` and having `testutils` import `drive` triggers an import cycle (Go treats `drive`'s internal `_test.go` files → `testutils` → `drive` as circular, even though it's only the non-test `drive` package). So I decoupled it by duplicating the tiny config-dir computation (`os.UserConfigDir()/paper-scan-processor`) directly in `testutils/drive.go`, with a comment explaining why, rather than exporting `configDir`. Build, vet, and `go test ./...` all pass.

Moving it to a file within `backend/drive` won't actually fix the cycle — the problem is at the package level, not the file level. `configDir()` would still be in package `drive`, so `testutils` importing it to call `configDir()` reintroduces the same cycle (drive's test files → testutils → drive).

There are two real ways to avoid both the cycle and the duplication:

- `backend/pdftest/pdftest.go` → `backend/pdf/testutils.go` (now `package pdf`) — `WritePDF`/`AssertOrder` are ordinary exported functions in the `pdf` package. `pdf_test.go` calls them unqualified (same package); `app_test.go` and `filetree_test.go` call them as `pdf.WritePDF`/`pdf.AssertOrder` via the import they already had for the package.
- `backend/drive/testutils_test.go` — restored essentially as it was (unexported `skipUnlessEnabled`, calling package-private `configDir()` directly, no cross-package dependency, no export needed).

No shared `testutils` package, no duplicated folder-name logic, no import cycle.
